scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Dancing the Disease: The Trance Rituals of Vimbuza
This is Vimbuza healing dance. Mid-19th century; UNESCO inscribed 2008.
on_screen: Title card: Vimbuza healing dance · Malawi · Mid-19th century; UNESCO inscribed 2008

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Vimbuza emerged among the Tumbuka of northern Malawi, eastern Zambia, and southern Tanzania during the nineteenth century, shaped by the Ngoni migrations known as the Mfecane and the convergence of Bemba, Bisa, Chewa, and Ngoni populations.
It developed partly as a replacement for mwavi, the poison ordeal suppressed by colonial authorities.
The Livingstonia Mission and colonial administrators instituted a formal ban around 1924 following a meeting at Elangeni in January 1920.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Vimbuza is performed when an individual is diagnosed with spirit possession causing mental or physical illness, understood as an imbalance of hot and cold forces.
Predominantly involving women, the ritual functions as both medical treatment and a socially accepted release within patrilineal and virilocal marriage systems.
A secondary, profane form featuring satirical songs (vigerembo or vigetyo) also developed to air social criticisms.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The healing process involves structured stages.
In kubunyisela, the patient sits concealed under a blanket in a hut while an assistant (musamu) coaxes the possessing spirits to state their names.
Once named, the patient is dressed in specific ritual attire and ankle bells.
Watch for Kubunyisela trance seating, Chilopa blood ritual.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Women and children form a circle around the patient

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Instrumental accompaniment is provided exclusively by drums carved from mubale wood, typically the large ng'oma yikulu and the smaller mphiningu, with Rumphi districts adding a third slower drum called mboza.
Historically, Ngoni dancers used a basin-shaped dried cattle hide called an ingubhu or clashing war shields.
Listen for the ng'oma yikulu, mphiningu, mboza, ingubhu.

Two or three mubale-wood drums—the large ng'oma yikulu and smaller mphiningu—provide deep, far-carrying percussion audible for several kilometres. This is layered with ringing iron ankle bells and a powerful call-and-response vocal exchange between a solo possessed dancer and a surrounding chorus of singing women and children.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Séances take place in a village house run by a healer, known as a temphiri.

Costumes vary by gender: men wear feathered njukula headdresses, kabudula shorts, arm feathers, and goatskin flaps (madumbo, zamba, or nyisi), while women wear duku headcloths, handkerchiefs, bracelets, and goatskin skirts.
Both wear mangwanda or mangenjeza iron ankle bells.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Boston Soko (Tumbuka researcher who documented the tradition), Steven Friedson (ethnomusicologist who studied and danced Vimbuza), John M. Janzen (scholar of the ngoma tradition), Victor Turner (scholar of Ndembu drums of affliction), Robert Laws (Scottish missionary of Livingstonia Mission), Donald Fraser (Scottish missionary).
Practised chiefly among the Tumbuka people of northern Malawi, as well as among related communities in eastern Zambia and southern Tanzania.

Vimbuza belongs to the broader ngoma ('drums of affliction') therapeutic complex found across Bantu-speaking Africa, sharing historical and structural ties with similar possession and healing traditions in central and southern Africa.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Vimbuza is a sacred healing ritual involving spirit possession and blood sacrifice; outsiders must approach with deep respect and avoid filming or disrupting healing ceremonies.

Costumes vary by gender: men wear feathered njukula headdresses, kabudula shorts, arm feathers, and goatskin flaps (madumbo, zamba, or nyisi), while women wear duku headcloths, handkerchiefs, bracelets, and goatskin skirts.
